text:
Emma (Product): Heads-up — planning a small pricing experiment to introduce a 'Flex' packaging option that sits between PAYG and Reserved. want to debate sequencing + launch criteria.
Devon (Sales): curious what 'Flex' means here — committed spend with elastic burst? or pure usage with softer rate limits?
Emma (Product): thinking: customers can commit a modest monthly baseline for discounted unit price + automatic burst capacity at higher per-unit rates. goal: capture teams that need predictability but don't want long contracts.
Liam (Eng): technically doable. main infra work: quota enforcement + billing hooks + burst autoscale policy. estimate ~3 dev-weeks + 2 infra-weeks to make it safe for beta.
Sofia (ML): also need to define model routing rules for Flex traffic (prefer cheaper quantized variants unless latency-critical). that affects perceived quality.
Maria (Finance): need revenue model. proposal: baseline commit = 30% discount vs PAYG, burst rate = 10% premium over PAYG. run numbers on churn risk.
Devon (Sales): from GTM side, target mid-market customers who currently reserve small capacity or overpay PAYG. can offer 3-month beta with flexible cancel.
Emma (Product): try prioritization using RICE quickly? impact = high for mid-market expansion, reach = 15 accounts in Q2, confidence = 0.6, effort = 5 (t-shirt). RICE score rough calc inline: Reach*Impact*Confidence/Effort -> 15*8*0.6/5 = 14.4.
Maria (Finance): those are optimistic. if reach is 15 and ARPA uplift is small, payback may be slow. recommend run A/B pilot with 10 customers for 2 months.
Liam (Eng): sequencing options: (A) build full Flex product with billing + routing + console controls (8 wks). (B) soft-launch via manual ops + priority tags + billing hacks (2-3 wks). we can validate demand faster with B.
Sofia (ML): option B still needs clear guardrails so Flex users don't get routed to low-quality models unexpectedly. we can add a 'latency-sensitive' flag per route for safety. low effort.
Emma (Product): I like B for discovery. launch criteria for wider rollout: 1) 10 paying customers in pilot, 2) <5% error/incidents attributable to Flex routing, 3) positive NPS delta or explicit renewal intent from >40% of pilots.
Devon (Sales): can commit 6 pilot candidates this week. need collateral: comparison table vs Reserved/PAYG + suggested sales script.
Maria (Finance): also need a cancellation/metering flow defined for accounting. if someone cancels mid-month, how do we prorate baseline vs burst? OpsBot: Billing policy template created at /policies/billing/prorate-flex-v1.md (automated).
Liam (Eng): for beta we can fake prorates with manual credits, but we should capture events for future automation. logs: we need to emit `flex.commit`, `flex.burst` events.
Emma (Product): ok action items: Emma to own pilot design + success metrics, Liam to prototype manual enforcement and event logging, Maria to model pricing sensitivity and finalize discount tiers, Devon to recruit pilot customers, Sofia to add routing safety flags. 2-week check-in?
Devon (Sales): noted. I'll start outreach and surface a simple ROI sheet for customers.
Sofia (ML): quick note on quality monitoring — add per-route evals for pilot to detect regressions against PAYG baseline. two automated tests should suffice.
Maria (Finance): will simulate revenue with three scenarios (low/med/high uptake) and share by Fri.
Liam (Eng): one more thing — rate-limit semantics: do we implement hard token bucket limits per minute, or soft throttling with 429s? for Flex I recommend a soft limit + queue with burst credits first. easier to roll back.
Emma (Product): agree soft-first. final question: should we tie Flex to specific region/tiers initially? maybe limit to hosted regions to avoid private infra complexity.
Devon (Sales): yes limit to hosted + dedicated lite. don't promise Private or on-prem yet.
Emma (Product): cool. I'll draft pilot spec and post here by EOD. thanks all. :rocket:
Liam (Eng): ack.
OpsBot: Reminder — create pilot feature flag: `pricing:flex_pilot` before any customer enrollments.
